what_happened: The job to add a reading-coverage check that scores each request bullet by its own words was rejected at the final verdict. One of 10 acceptance criteria was unmet: the one saying the change refuses more readings, that the higher refusal rate is intended, and that the replay test or its output states the measured rate over recorded requests. There were two major findings and no blockers. First, the bullet extraction (request_acceptance_bullets in coverage.rs) reads an `Acceptance:` heading inside quoted evidence such as code fences, so a request can be checked against another job's bullets. Second, the CHANGELOG entry and a doc comment misstate the replay by presenting job 1fva as a real omission. No checks are listed as failed.
cause: The parser and its claims were built from the shape of the request wording and a few hand-picked cases. Nothing required the new rule to run over the recorded real requests, including ones that quote other jobs' text in code fences, before the final verdict. The replay's actual result was never checked against what the changelog and comments said about it. Because the producer is not required to run the replay over recorded requests and report its measured rate and any mismatches, the parsing flaw, the missing rate evidence and the misstated claim were all found only by the verifier. This is the same gap as the two earlier cases in this class.
prevention: Make a replay over the recorded real requests a required step of any job that adds or changes a refusal or matching rule. The step runs the old and new builds over all recorded requests and writes a record with the measured newly-refused count and rate, the requests whose parsed bullets differ from the raw text, and the newly refused readings. The producer must run it and check that its changelog and comment claims match the output. The verifier then reads that record instead of trusting an estimate. The replay must include requests that quote other jobs' text in code fences, so evidence blocks cannot be read as the request's own bullets.
proposed_request: Fix the reading-coverage check from job 20261110-124307-bn3c so it lands. Outcome: the check judges a request only on that request's own acceptance bullets. Text inside quoted evidence, such as code fences or block quotes, never counts as the request's Acceptance heading or bullets. Add a test using a request that quotes another job's request with its own Acceptance heading inside a code fence; the check must use only the outer request's bullets. Run the check over all recorded requests and readings with the old and new builds, and put the measured number and rate of newly refused readings in the replay test output (cargo test -p athena-core -- --nocapture). The replay must show that no newly refused reading covers all its bullets. State that measured rate in the changelog in place of the 10% estimate. Correct the CHANGELOG.md entry and the doc comment near coverage.rs lines 324-326 so they describe what the replay shows for job 1fva, and do not call it a real omission unless the recorded request and reading show one. Keep the existing criteria; cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test must pass.
